note: Track keys, step 6: a chorus moved up a whole step, heard, worked out as the same numbers in the new key on two key-chords panels, then prepared with the new key's 5th chord. The key is moves (any key): the backing tracks are written as numerals so they follow it, the chorus is counted the long way once as chord tokens, and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same.

exercise.title: Up a step for the last chorus
exercise.why: Every chord of the chorus moves up by the same whole step, so its numbers stay the same in the new key, and the new key's 5th chord played just before it makes the lift sound prepared.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track: a chorus in {{=key}}, played twice, then the same chorus a whole step up.
Listen for the bar where everything lifts, and call out "up" there.
Practice until you can call it with your eyes away from the chord boxes.

The chorus is four chords. {{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, {{chord:V}} the 5th chord, built on {{5}}, {{chord:vi}} the 6th chord, built on {{6}}, and {{chord:IV}} the 4th chord, built on {{4}}.
Press those four in that order in the first row below, the chords of {{=key}} major. Then press the same four numbers in the second row, the key a whole step up.
Practice until you can say the chorus in the new key without reading it.

Press Play below to start the backing track. This time the last bar in {{=key}} is {{chord:VI7}}, the 5th chord of the new key, so the lift is announced one bar early.
Look away from the chord boxes and call out "up" on the first bar of the new key.
Then pick a chorus you know and name the 5th chord that would lift it a whole step.
{{?key}}In another key the chords have other names, and the lift is still a whole step, with the new key's 5th chord one bar before it.
